domain_guidance.summary: This primary domain focuses extensively on patient assessment techniques, detailed physical examinations, and collecting extensive health history data while holding a distinct weight of 32.0 percent on the overall certification examination.

This specific diagnostic domain covers advanced clinical reasoning and detailed differential diagnosis strategies for a wide variety of medical conditions with an assigned exam weight of exactly 26.5 percent.

This planning domain directly addresses effective treatment planning, appropriate antibiotic stewardship, and evidence-based therapeutic interventions, accounting for a substantial weight of precisely 26.5 percent on the board examination.

This final evaluation domain involves monitoring ongoing patient progress and carefully evaluating clinical outcomes to ensure high standards of care, representing a focused weight of 15.0 percent on the complete test.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Manage your pacing carefully across all 150 questions during the official 180-minute testing window. Read every single clinical scenario carefully and evaluate all available choices before submitting your final answers.

faq.answer_text: The test contains exactly 150 questions distributed across four distinct domains covering clinical assessment, medical diagnosis, treatment planning, and outcome evaluation for family nurse practitioners.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: You should check directly with the American Academy of Nurse Practitioners Certification Board (AANPCB) for specific score requirements and official passing standards for this certification.
Candidates are given a total duration of 180 minutes to complete the entire assessment and answer all of the clinical questions presented during the testing session.

The American Academy of Nurse Practitioners Certification Board (AANPCB) is the official organization that administers, governs, and manages the family nurse practitioner credential along with its associated certification examinations and credentialing requirements.

editorial.overview: The AANP Family Nurse Practitioner Certification (FNP-C) is administered by the American Academy of Nurse Practitioners Certification Board (AANPCB) to validate your professional clinical competence effectively during the testing window. This complete assessment covers four core domains: assessment, diagnosis, planning, and evaluation across a total of 150 questions to measure clinical knowledge accurately.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review clinical guidelines and study the four domain weights carefully before your test date. Practice answering challenging clinical questions that test your assessment and diagnosis skills completely. Focus intently on patient evaluation techniques and detailed treatment planning strategies over the 180 minutes of simulated testing time.
editorial.who_should_take: Nurse practitioners seeking board certification to practice as family nurse practitioners should take this test. Candidates need clinical experience and graduate-level family nurse practitioner education.
